fonte: Johnston et al., Medical Journal of Australia, 2017 (ASP-20)
texto_para_tela: 23 DEATHS · JULY 2005–JUNE 2015 · 17 BROWN SNAKES · 0 INLAND TAIPAN
credito_sugerido: Source: Johnston et al., Medical Journal of Australia, 2017 (ASP-20)
nota: Relidos no texto integral e no resumo. PENDENTE f114, ACHADO: 'ten followed out-of-hospital cardiac arrests' (resumo) e 'Out-of-hospital cardiac arrest was the most common cause of death (ten cases), followed by intracranial haemorrhage (six cases)' (resultados). N006: as mortes juntam o ASP e o NCIS ('Box 3 – Details for 23 deaths attributed to snakebite, recorded by the Australian Snakebite Project (ASP) or the National Coronial Information System (NCIS)'). Se as dez paradas forem à tela: '10 OF 23 AFTER CARDIAC ARREST OUTSIDE HOSPITAL', com o mesmo crédito e período.

grafias_do_espelho: Source: Johnston et al., Medical Journal of Australia, 2017 (ASP-20)
texto_aprovado: A separate national study of snakebites, from 2005 to 2015, counted 23 deaths. Seventeen were put down to brown snakes. None was put down to the inland taipan. For a country with so many venomous snakes, that toll is small.
